title: Is the rabbit closer to the lower hundred or the higher one?
description: Meera's rabbit sits at the same spot, but now the food is one hundred apart. The video counts the jumps each way to find the nearest hundred.
teaching_notes: One idea: the nearest hundred also comes from counting jumps both ways. Watch for a child who looks only at the last digit and ignores the tens digit.

source: The rabbit is at 2,346 and its food is at 2,300 and 2,400. W
video_script.why: The child has found the nearest ten, but not the nearest hundred where the jumps are many more.
video_script.substitution: Count the jumps down and up to the two hundreds and choose the fewer.
video_script.anchor: Meera's pet rabbit hopping along a numbered garden path in Pune
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu looks at the last digit six and says go up. The last digit only decides the nearest ten; the jumps to the hundreds must be counted.
video_script.payoff_line: forty six jumps is fewer than fifty four jumps

final_answer.value: 2,300 is the nearest hundred of 2,346, with 46 jumps
final_answer.spoken: two thousand three hundred with forty six jumps

maths_rules: your turn: rabbit at 5,274, food at 5,200 and 5,300; 5,274 − 5,200 = 74 and 5,300 − 5,274 = 26; 26 < 74 so 5,300; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: count the jumps both ways. The same rabbit and path stay as the anchor; the number line is longer and its ticks are shown at tens.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the garden path with the rabbit sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a garden path with a rabbit at 2,346 and two far food bowls at 2,300 and 2,400

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='rabbit'/>Meera's rabbit is back on its garden path in Pune, at two thousand three hundred and forty six.
<bookmark mark='food'/>This time the food is far away, at two thousand three hundred and at two thousand four hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which food is closer, and how many jumps away is it?

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a long number line from 2,300 to 2,400 with the rabbit at 2,346; the ticks are shown only at every ten to keep it clear

marks.line: the number line from 2,300 to 2,400 appears with the rabbit at 2,346
marks.jump: a small arc shows one jump from 2,346 to 2,347

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>The path is longer now, from one food to the other.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>The rabbit still moves one number at a time, so every jump counts.
<bookmark mark='def'/>The hundred with the fewest jumps is called the nearest hundred.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows the last digit 6 circled with the words six is big; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the last digit 6 circled
marks.count: two jump counters appear and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The last digit is six, which is big, so the rabbit goes up.
<bookmark mark='far'/>That digit only tells the jumps to the next ten, not to the next hundred.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Only counting the jumps both ways can decide.

beats.on_screen: the board shows the jumps down: 2,346 − 2,300 = 46

marks.down: the jumps down are drawn on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='down'/>Count the jumps down to the food on the left.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Two thousand three hundred and forty six take away two thousand three hundred leaves forty six.

beats.on_screen: the board shows the jumps up: 2,400 − 2,346 = 54, then both counts side by side

marks.up: the jumps up are drawn on the line
marks.pay: 46 and 54 glow side by side and the bowl at 2,300 is lit; the card 2,300 is the nearest hundred appears

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Next, count the jumps up to the food on the right.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Two thousand four hundred take away two thousand three hundred and forty six leaves fifty four.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Forty six jumps is fewer than fifty four jumps, so the rabbit goes to two thousand three hundred.

beats.on_screen: two lines: count the jumps down and up; the fewer jumps win; then a rabbit at 5,274 with food at 5,200 and 5,300 and an empty box

<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. A rabbit sits at five thousand two hundred and seventy four.
<bookmark mark='food'/>Food waits at five thousand two hundred, and at five thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='q'/>Which is the nearest hundred?
